Rural healthcare is essential in #CO03, and today is a reminder of the people who keep it running. I’ve seen their work up close, and I’m committed to strengthening these services so every family can access the care they deserve. #NationalRuralHealthDay https://t.co/877F3pnxFa

The Affordable Care Act simply isn’t affordable, and health insurance premiums are spiking. Families in #CO03 shouldn’t be hit by a system that’s already failing them.

I’m part of a bipartisan group outlining a practical path forward on health care. Our bill, the Bipartisan HOPE Act, prevents those immediate hikes while adding real guardrails and accountability. It’s a bridge that gives Congress the space to take on the real issue: underlying health care costs that keep rising year after year.

The ACA hasn’t lived up to its name, but letting premiums jump overnight isn’t an option. I’m focused on helping families now and pushing for long-term reforms that actually lower costs. That’s the work ahead.

Read my full release on the Bipartisan HOPE Act here: https://t.co/JJwZExPAaR

Healthcare costs don’t care about party or geography. Families in rural and urban communities across #CO03 are feeling the squeeze.

I joined 34 Republican and Democrat colleagues to launch CommonGround 2025, a bipartisan plan to extend premium tax credits, set reasonable income caps, and crack down on fraud. This is especially important for ranchers, small business owners, and self-employed Coloradans in the individual market.

Healthcare affordability is a solvable problem when we work together. #CommonGround2025

In my first year in Congress, I’ve seen intense media and think-tank scrutiny of Republican reforms to Medicaid, and our efforts to preserve the system for the most vulnerable while reining in skyrocketing spending.

What gets far less attention is a harder but more important question: what are we actually getting for those dollars?

Good public policy doesn’t stop at inputs. It looks at outcomes. It asks (and verifies) whether programs are delivering real results for the people they’re meant to serve. Shockingly, in health care—and especially in Medicaid—that kind of scrutiny is often missing.

This reporting underscores why that matters. When Medicaid fraud, waste, and abuse go unchecked, taxpayers lose trust, vulnerable patients are shortchanged, and resources are diverted away from real care.

Protecting Medicaid means being serious about accountability: so the program is sustainable, effective, and worthy of the people it’s supposed to help.
